atomRelations.basis: The composite definition refines the named type-level morpheme category.
The formation claim adds the carrier-plus-content condition to the composite definition.
The graphological limitation excludes graphemes from the full carrier alternative.
The notation claim requires the documentary representation to preserve symbiosis.
The compact notation refines how symbiotic representation is recorded in the lessons.
Carrier shorthand may omit displayed content only as understood documentation.
The carrier-only warning prevents documentary shorthand from redefining the morpheme.
A portmanteau morpheme is the content-cluster subtype of the composite category.
The cluster condition requires indivisible sememes without separately analyzable carriers.
Carrier and content elements retain their linguistic identities through cooperation in morphemes.
The three-kind inventory partitions morphemes by symbiotic carrier-content structure.
The connective class realizes the sound-plus-no-sememic-meaning inventory member.
The grammatical-meaning claim distinguishes absence of a sememe from absence of grammatical function.
The ordinary class realizes the phoneme-unit-plus-sememe-unit inventory member.
The English example evidences coexistence of ordinary morphemes without authorizing a Classical Source.
The silent class realizes the sigeme-plus-sememe-unit inventory member.
Linguistic economy licenses silent expression where phonological expenditure is unnecessary.
The economy rule applies when a culture treats the information as a default absent contrary indication.
